Why It Matters Who Shows Up

You're Hiring Vince, Not A Call Center

TRC is Vince Taylor and a two-man crew. That is the whole company, on purpose. Vince walks your bathroom, prices it himself, and is on site every day it is being built — so there is no salesman who vanishes after the contract, no rotating parade of subs, and nobody to pass the blame to when a detail is wrong. Brian in Rock Hill said it plainly after his 1980s master and hall baths were rebuilt: Vince and his two assistants were on site each day, not a random parade of workers.

Talk To Vince

How We Build

The TRC Effect

Same approach on a small guest bath as on a full master suite: get the parts you never see right, and the parts you do see take care of themselves.

Waterproofing before anything pretty happens

Every custom shower gets a waterproof membrane, a properly sloped pan and full substrate prep before the first tile goes up. It is the least photogenic day of the job and the one that decides whether your shower is still sound in twenty years.

The part most contractors leave out of the quote

  1. One crew, start to finish

    Vince and the same two sets of hands every day — never a rotating cast of subs.

  2. Cleaned up daily

    Floors protected, debris carried out, and the room left usable wherever the stage of work allows.

  3. A written scope before demo starts

    You know what is included, what it costs, and roughly how long it takes before anything comes off the wall.

Only tile that belongs in a wet space

Not every tile is built for a shower. We specify porcelain and ceramic with low water absorption, seal the grout properly, and show you how to keep it that way. No guesswork on materials, and no surprises two winters later.

Done right the first time

Vince has personally torn out and rebuilt dozens of showers that other contractors got wrong. That is the entire reason TRC works the way it does — the cheapest bid is almost never the cheapest job. If something is not right on ours, we come back and make it right.

Our Work

Recent Bathrooms We've Built

Bathroom Remodeling In The Carolinas

Custom Tiled Showers In Fort Mill & Rock Hill

Most of what we get called for starts the same way: a builder-grade tub-and-surround nobody actually uses, or a garden tub eating half the room. Taking it out and building a proper walk-in shower in its place changes how the entire bathroom works — and it is the single upgrade homeowners here tell us they wish they had done sooner.

We build custom tiled showers to any size, shape or slope, from a 48-inch square in a guest bath to a full master with a freestanding soaker and a separate glass enclosure. When the timeline matters more than the tile, acrylic and composite wall systems go in over about two days with almost no dust and no weeks of demo.

  • Custom tiled showers to any size, shape or slope
  • Tub-to-shower conversions, including low-entry and grab-bar layouts
  • Frameless glass, door-less panels, bench seats and recessed niches
  • Two-day acrylic and composite systems when time is the constraint

FAQs

Frequently asked

How long does a bathroom remodel with a custom tiled shower take?

Most bathroom remodels with a custom tiled shower run a few weeks, and the exact schedule depends on the size of the room, the materials you pick and how much plumbing or electrical has to move. You get a realistic timeline in writing before demo starts, and updates as the job moves.

Can I get a written estimate before any work begins?

Yes. Vince comes out, walks the space, talks through your ideas and puts a recommended scope of work in writing so you can make decisions with real numbers. There is no pressure and no deposit required to book the consultation.

What's the difference between a custom-tiled shower and an acrylic system?

A custom-tiled shower gives you full control over size, shape, tile and finish — it is the right call when you want the bathroom to be a feature. An acrylic or composite wall system is quicker to install and lower maintenance, with a non-porous surface that resists mold and mildew. We will price both so you can compare honestly.

How does the two-day tub-to-shower conversion work?

We pull the old tub or surround, prep the space, and install the new low-entry base and wall system — typically over about two days with virtually no dust or mess. It is the option most people choose when they want the bathroom back quickly without weeks of construction.

What keeps a custom tile shower from leaking down the line?

Waterproof membranes, a properly sloped pan and careful substrate prep before a single tile goes up. Those three things direct water where it should go and protect the framing behind the walls — and they are exactly where a cheap bid usually cuts corners.

Can you build a shower for accessibility or aging in place?

Yes, and it is a large part of what we do. Low-entry and curbless bases, built-in bench seats, grab bars set into blocked walls, handheld fixtures and slip-resistant pan tile can all be designed in from the start rather than added on later.

Which areas do you serve?

We work out of Fort Mill and serve Rock Hill, Tega Cay, Indian Land and Lancaster on the South Carolina side, plus Ballantyne, Waxhaw, Weddington, Indian Trail, Mint Hill, Matthews and Pineville across the North Carolina line. Licensed in both states, so the line is not a problem.
